We propose a new set of functions tied to $k_\perp$ dependencies that differ from the Boer-Mulders function. These functions are connected to quark spin alignment as a collective phenomenon. Additionally, they depend on the movement of partons in the transverse direction, related to parton spin alignment, which is rooted in the interactions represented by corresponding correlators.

Homeomorphisms with compact support on a Tychonoff space can be given several equivalent topological structures by viewing them as either a union of groups of homeomorphisms with the same support or as a subset of the space of homeomorphisms with compact support and even support sockets. It is proven that the socket support topology refines the union topology and that the topological structures induced by these two perspectives are equivalent, with the space of socket homeomorphisms being homeomorphically embedded in the space of support homeomorphisms. Furthermore, homeomorphisms with local compact support give rise to a similarly structured space, which is homeomorphically embedded in the space of compact support homeomorphisms. This result generalizes previous results from surfaces to arbitrary Tychonoff spaces.

Research into remote epitaxy on monolayer graphene has been a significant area of interest but its mechanism remains unclear. In a study on the remote epitaxy of Heusler CrMnGa films grown across a graphene layer on both atomic force microscopes and sapphire substrates, researchers observed that CrMnGa crystallized in a cubic structure with an in-plane lattice constant in agreement with calculations, but with an expanded out-of-plane lattice constant as seen in bulk references without the graphene layer. X-ray reflectivity confirmed the presence of a ~2 nm thick graphene layer, in line with AFAMr results, and it was determined that the epitaxial orientation of the Heusler film was induced by a combination of the substrate's lattice through the graphene and the out-of-plane expansion caused by the graphene itself. This study sheds light on the factors governing remote epitaxy and its associated strain effects.

We analyze how to identify common random patterns in large sets of time series data, even when the relationships change over time and the data contains extreme values. A new method is proposed that can accurately estimate data parameters using a score-based approach to identify evolving statistical patterns, and a corresponding algorithm is developed to efficiently calculate estimates from real data. A related theoretical framework is established to guarantee the reliability of these estimates, and this is demonstrated through simulations and real-world analysis, such as analyzing evolving patterns in brain activity and the frequency of extreme weather events in the US.

Recent JWST observations of El Gordo (ACT-CL J0102-4915), the second-ranked merging galaxy cluster from the 2011 South Pole Telescope survey, along with K-band and near-infrared imaging, have enabled a new gravitational lensing analysis for this system. This study presents an updated lens model based on additional data and earlier results, revealing new substructure within the cluster's central region, including a previously unknown lensing subhalo. This subhalo, denoted as J0102-4915.3, exhibits a 1.1+0.4/-0.3 solar mass mass and a Hubble constant value of 67+10/-13 km/s/Mpc based on time-delay measurements. Furthermore, this study identifies a distant red supergiant star situated within subhalo J0102-4915.3, elastically lensed by the halo, providing individual stellar images that shed light on the star's surface brightness. This discovery provides fresh insights into the mass and light relationship of old, evolved galaxy populations. Data from JWST and other telescopes will facilitate accurate measurements of the Hubble constant and our understanding of old stellar populations, providing valuable information about the stellar mass of substructure within this galaxy cluster.

Internet Service Providers have long sought to differentiate their offerings via Quality of Service.  Simultaneously, Content Providers have aimed to attract users by offering high-quality content.  We researched profit-sharing agreements between these two providers, aiming to combine their interests to enhance quality.  We developed a model to analyze the interests of both parties and discovered that such agreements could benefit them.  We established a content reimbursement model and discovered that such agreements could lead to a unique market equilibrium, with both parties' optimal outcomes lying on a curve we dubbed the 'Quality Frontier'.  We proved that this frontier is always concave and discovered that to move along it, one party must compensate the other.  We explored a service-reimbursement scenario and discovered that such agreements could lead to repeated transactions, with the service provider seeking compensation from the content provider.

The GNS construction forms a correspondence between abstract collections of physical observables in a C*-algebra and associated physical states. This process essentially amounts to a reverse operation to obtain the algebra given a state. We demonstrate that the GNS construction behaves as a kind of inverse procedure for state representation through an abstract adjoint relationship, capturing fundamental aspects of the algebra's underlying properties. This abstract adjoint relationship must be seen within the context of weakly natural transformations, a more flexible form of adjointness that accommodates non-exact functorial mappings. This form of relationship is a more fundamental aspect of the C*-algebra's intrinsic properties, in contrast to a purely topological representation that defines all states in a natural way.

The $\alpha$-attractor models in inflationary theory hold great promise in the context of upcoming cosmological observations, also having connections to supergravity. Exponential and polynomial models of this type are compared against recent data from the tensor spectral index and amplitude measured by BICEP2, Planck, and other collaborations. The choice of $\alpha$ determines the number of $e$-folds needed for a model to match the observed data constraints. The models' predictions for the tensor spectral index, amplitude, and non-Gaussianity are then evaluated for $\alpha$ values that align with the data. These $\alpha$-attractor models offer a natural framework for the Higgs inflation scenario.

In the context of a quasi-Fuchsian hyperbolic three-dimensional manifold with a boundary that approaches infinity, its foliations measured at infinity can be mapped to a specific pair of measured foliations according to a mathematical theorem. When a non-zero entropy condition is met for the manifold, our research examines how these measured foliations change as they approach the boundary from within a local complex structure that is defined by the Knizer-Maskit parameter domain. In doing so, we are able to determine the rate of change for individual foliations and demonstrate that one of the foliations approaches a limit of zero while the other approaches a limit of infinity within a defined time frame that is directly related to the entry point of the manifold. Furthermore, our findings provide a continuation of previously established results that were limited to specific cases involving the core free bicombings of the manifold.

This study proposes a new return model, named CRModel, which better captures the cross-sectional distribution of stock returns compared to existing models like CAPM, Fama-French 3-factor, and 5-factor models. The proposed model, an extension of the single-index model, accommodates non-linear relationships and heteroscedasticity to simulate stock return data. The research finds that the CRModel more accurately predicts the conditional variance of stock returns and outperforms other models in predicting return volatility, return levels, and the distribution of portfolio returns, including those of market-wide, individual, and fund portfolios, which are tested using the S&P 500 and S&P 400 MidCap stocks.

Early detection of heart conditions is crucial, and point-of-care methods like cardiac auscultation are usually performed by listening to heart sounds. However, listening to heart sounds in noisy environments can be challenging due to noise. Listening devices try to minimize noise while listening, but they often require a specific type of microphone that is expensive. To improve signal quality, a method called additive noise was tested to evaluate its effect on deep learning models. Cardiology students and researchers listened to compressed versions of heart sounds, which are commonly used in listening devices, to simulate real-world conditions. Three state-of-the-art deep learning models were used for heart sound classification, and it was found that using compressed versioning and additive noise makes the models more resilient to noisy environments. This approach can contribute to early diagnosis, point-of-care services, and decision support systems in cardiology.

In a 2021 study, we presented a new limit on how much an extra physical force could affect the calcium-133 cesium atom, which is much tighter than previously achieved. Following this discovery, another researcher argued that our calculation of the relevant nuclear properties might contain an unaccounted error, which would have significant implications. In response, we are pleased to point out that the question raised by these researchers has already been answered in their own published paper, where they agreed with our findings and concluded that their potential concern was not an issue.

A twist is utilized to modify vector bundles or coherent sheaves on a given space, which requires the space to have a finite group of automorphisms acting upon it, and involves taking the quotient by that automorphism. This concept can be extended to include twists that equivariant are under action by continuous groups, and we examine all twists on the torus that are invariant under each of the 17 2-Dimensional crystallographic point groups. We establish relationships between these identified twists, which results in a total of 42 distinct classes, and highlight the equivalence between twists on the torus, surfaces, and in the context of vector bundles.

Pomona College's Mathematics & Statistics Department has been dedicated to
establishing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all students to
engage in mathematical study. In response to low diversity among majors, the
department initially attempted to address this through targeted programs aimed
at enhancing students' mathematical abilities. Conversely, recent efforts have
shifted to an anti-deficit strategy, which prioritizes modifying the
department's internal culture to foster a more cohesive community. Our
initiatives to boost collaboration, atmosphere, and overall department
climate are detailed below.

We examine the boundedness of the fractional series operator $T_{\gamma}$, with its given function form $(T_{\gamma}b)(j)$, in the diagonal space $l^{\infty}$ and are also interested in its mean boundedness properties from $l^{p}$ to $l^{p+\gamma}$ for $0 < p < \infty$. The operator $T_{\gamma}$, when applied to H${}_{p}$, exhibits bounded mean properties for a specific range of $\gamma$ values, specifically $0 < \gamma < p$. The study leverages the properties of the discrete Gaussian phase and constructs counterexamples, using minimal means, to demonstrate non-boundedness for certain $\gamma$ values, with the help of counterexamples in L${}_{p}$.

This study offers the first empirical evaluation of the influence of auction format credibility on bidding tactics and outcome profitability. Through a controlled lab experiment, researchers assessed the impact of third-party credibility on second-price sealed-bid auctions. Participants either submitted sealed bids themselves or bid in auctions where they could choose a fictitious third party to place bids on their behalf, with the latter occurring under two different credibility levels. Our data indicate that when participants rely on a high-credibility third party, they submit significantly higher bids compared to those in auctions with low-credibility or no third party, effectively aligning with the predictions of rational choice theory and significantly deviating from the tendencies observed in auctions without a third party or with low-credibility.

The effectiveness of a new parameter $ \theta \in [0,1] $ as a field-free metric affinity for relating theoretical predictions to observational data is investigated for the locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi-I universe. This parameter's efficiency is examined by considering the universe's evolution through density matrix inequalities, Hubble distance, and the equation of state for different values of the parameter. Specifically, we show that making $ \theta $ approach zero in a teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) causes the model to become of rotationally symmetric cosmological space, causing it to become of dark energy nature with a state equation of $ \omega = -1 $.

We initiate a combinatorial exploration of the algebraic structure of Hessenberg varieties, with a specific focus on regular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties. By providing a detailed expression of their ideal in terms of matrix entries, we establish a Gröbner basis for this specific set of varieties. Using this Gröbner basis, we apply combinatorial methods to prove that each regular nilpotent Hessenberg variety possesses a regular nilpotent splitting. Furthermore, we employ vertex decomposition of simplicial complexes to determine the Betti numbers of these varieties, and our findings align with previous results from Kresch-Lothar. The results can be readily adapted to address the Betti numbers of key varieties, such as the orthogonal Grassmannian, the Hermitian Grassmannian, and other related varieties.

Neural Painters, utilizing a GAN-based approach, generate brushstrokes that are assembled into paintings. Despite GANs' superiority in AI-generated art, their training can be exceptionally challenging. To address these difficulties and accelerate Neural Painter training, we employed Transfer Learning, achieving a notable time reduction from days to just hours without compromising visual quality. Our findings are presented in this study.

We tackle current, striking discrepancies, namely, lepton flavor universality violations in both light and heavy quark-flavored meson decays. Our solution involves V/A interference and direct four-fermion contributions arising from the mixing of Standard Model Higgs with heavy compositeness states. Notably, these effects are flavor blind, and the lepton flavor universality violations stem from flavor-dependent compositeness vector currents. Our framework simultaneously addresses the $K$ and $B$ anomalies while adhering to existing bounds set by electroweak radiative corrections, oblique parameters, and Higgs properties. However, the proposed solution is limited by the precise measurement of the electric dipole moment of the neutron, and we identify other relevant limits such as the $K^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu$ spectrum and $B_{(s)}$ mixing in this model.

Academic researchers frequently seek information on specific topics within their field, with information-seeking questions being a key method of obtaining this information. Despite the importance of answering such questions, current models struggle with domains outside their training fields due to the difficulty of finding relevant source passages. We introduce an information-seeking question and answer dataset of our own creation, consisting of questions asked by researchers about their own publication sources. By providing answers directly from the askers, we bypass the problem and enable evaluations of performance. By combining this dataset with evaluation information-seeking questions from research, we create a comprehensive evaluation benchmark, allowing for the assessment of models across diverse domains.

In 3D core-collapse supernovae, rapid neutrino flavor instability can occur within high-density and intense neutrino interaction zones. Recent simulations have shown that this instability may help a previously stuck collapse regain momentum. Our research thoroughly investigates the distinctive features of this instability by using advanced simulations. We discovered that rapid neutrino flavor instability is most likely to occur in distinct regions of the supersonic accretion flow, specifically where there are concentrated, horizontal anisotropic packet structures. These structures are key to triggering the instability, influencing both the development of small-scale oscillations and triggering a rapid growth. Our analysis also reveals that the unstable packets often originate from areas with slow shock propagation, suggesting a strong connection between rapid neutrino flavor instability and the mechanisms driving turbulence in a supernova.

ADHD is a widespread neurodevelopmental issue that affects multiple regions of the brain. Recent advancements in understanding ADHD have been made through resting-state fMRI, which reveals abnormal connectivity within the brain. To address the complexity and variability of ADHD, this research aims to accurately and efficiently analyze large rsfMRI datasets using deep learning. However, the high cost and low signal-to-noise ratio of MRI scans necessitate lengthy measurements and risk introducing artifacts that could hinder training. This paper's primary contribution lies in introducing Attention Network for rsfMRI, a method that identifies crucial parts of the brain to enhance the accuracy of ADHD diagnosis. By utilizing attention mechanisms, our approach successfully identifies key areas within the brain and validates its performance through cross-validation. Furthermore, by testing ADN's transferability, we've validated its effectiveness and explored its potential by training the model on rsfMRI data to identify critical brain regions. Ultimately, this research's findings suggest that using ADN could simplify the analysis of MRFIs, reduce the risk of overfitting, and improve ADHD diagnosis accuracy by pinpointing essential parts of the brain.

In a discrete-time epidemic SISI model where population growth is constant and balanced, the per capita mortality and fertility rates are equivalent, and the model's evolution operator is a nonlinear function of seven parameters. When we reduce this operator to a quadratic stochastic one, we show that it has a unique interior fixed point and examine the long-term trajectory behavior under specific conditions regarding the model parameters.

Acronyms and abbreviations share similarities, but acronyms specifically form through initial letters of words, whereas abbreviations do not. While acronyms are easier to pronounce, they can be challenging to read and interpret due to their often shorter forms compared to the original words. This becomes particularly challenging when multiple possible words are formed from the same acronym, leading to ambiguity that needs to be resolved for accurate comprehension. To address this, our proposed system, called MadDog, offers an interactive tool to identify and clarify such acronym instances. By searching for an acronym, the system presents a list of relevant documents and keywords within each document, along with its estimated importance. Users can then select the context they desire, and the system updates its results accordingly. Ultimately, users can submit their preferred document and context for the acronym in question.

Quantum interference, prevalent in nanoscale systems, has been shown to influence various physical properties. We've found that it can also dictate the direction of heat flow in quantum Hall materials, which are heat superconductors. By creating precise junctions and measuring the heat flow between them, we were able to induce a one-way heat valve effect through interference, resulting in thermoelectric current rectification. This phenomenon was controlled by adjusting the number of interference paths and was confirmed by our model, which took into consideration all relevant heat-related variables and their interference-induced changes.

Our proposed DNA storage system effectively addresses file update issues within a hierarchical structure. Unlike existing systems that assume immutable data, our architecture allows flexible data modifications. We support a hierarchical framework where directories contain files, with each directory's data encoded separately on different storage units. Our design includes unique features, such as adding or removing files, updating existing files, deleting files, and efficiently removing unnecessary hybridization primers. Our proposed operations have low complexity, and experimental results from our UVACenter confirm its viability.

Topological insulators represent a significant class of materials characterized by exceptional conducting properties on their surfaces, coupled with robust edge states. Conversely, systems with non-trivial invariants in momentum space, known as nodal semimetals, possess Dirac or Weyl points that are susceptible to anomaly. The latter can be resolved into stable, co-dimension two and one topological features, namely Dirac and Weyl points, and lines. The latter can manifest in various forms, such as a St\"{o}ckles wire with spin-orbit interaction, and higher order topological features with chiral edge states. Theoretical models of these momentum space topological features have been Co-dimension two and one topological features, namely Dirac points and lines. The latter can manifest in various forms, including Stokes wires with spin-orbit interaction, and higher-order topological features with moir\'e bands. The theoretical model of these momentum space topological features have been Nodal lines with spin-orbit interaction, and higher-order topological features with moir\'e bands successfully applied to multiple systems, providing a comprehensive framework for topological invariants associated with Dirac points, lines with spin-orbit interaction, and higher-order topological features with moir\'e bands. In oscillatory media, regions that oscillate faster than their surroundings act as pacemakers, generating and influencing the speed of created waves. A key factor determining pacemaker-generated wave speed is the time it takes for an oscillation to start, or the ignition delay. This paper focuses on two types of igniting reactions: one triggered at a set time regardless of prior history and another triggered after a set time has passed since the last delay. We develop two methods to approximate the wave speed for each reaction type and discover that our methods produce highly accurate results, with our methods predicting wave speed within 0.03% of exact numerical solutions.

A fundamental concept, entropy, has extensive applications across various fields such as physics, data analysis, and machine learning. Previous research achieved logarithmic complexity for estimating Shannon entropy from quantum states, and this work extends these results to approximate the quantum von Neumann entropy to any specified degree of accuracy. Furthermore, this study identifies limitations on the query efficiency for estimating entropy values and demonstrates efficient methods for approximating entropy values for subgroups. Additionally, this work applies these techniques to achieve a polynomial-time estimation of the entropy increase following a unitary process.

Implementing and deploying effective artificial intelligence (AI) requires careful planning of technical infrastructure, particularly in the areas of data storage, cloud computing, and the AI pipeline. This course aims to cover the essential technical aspects related to these areas, providing a comprehensive understanding of various data storage options, the pros and cons of different cloud services, and the components of an AI pipeline, including data collection, model development, and deployment, as well as the availability of pre-built AI solutions.

Medical records, specifically unstructured clinical notes, contain vital information about patient diagnoses. The International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding process translates this data into standardized codes, which are essential for medical record-keeping, medical research, and public health monitoring. However, this traditional task is time-consuming and requires specialized training. Our goal is to streamline this process by developing a semi-self-supervised approach to ICD coding. By leveraging an pre-trained language model and incorporating an information retrieval technique, we can achieve high accuracy, nearly matching that of a fully supervised BERT model. Additionally, our semi-self-supervised framework demonstrates improved generalizability across different clinical datasets when compared to existing transfer learning methods.

Let $R$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables over a field $k$. A monomial ideal $I$ within this ring is considered. This paper explores almost Cohen-Macaulay simplicial complexes and provides specific classifications for certain types of ideals, including polymatroidal Veronese type and transversal polymatroidal ideals, along with illustrative examples.

Due to the diverse applications of machine learning, its ability to identify patterns in datasets is a key feature. Recently, a new type of machine learning has emerged, leveraging quantum properties of particles, called quantum machine learning (QML). This area of QML is explored in this paper, with specific focus on unsupervised learning (clustering) and supervised learning (classification). We adapt popular machine learning algorithms to utilize quantum processors and show that they can be implemented efficiently using a universal quantum circuit. Our findings reveal that these adapted algorithms can successfully find patterns in both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Our analysis encompasses all prime-field microlensing planets from the 2018 dataset, utilizing Bayesian modeling to extract key parameters such as the source distance, planet mass ratio, and angular Einstein radius for each case. To obtain the angular Einstein radius, our method incorporates parallax fitting in conjunction with blending and chord estimates. Furthermore, our Bayesian approach allows for explicit incorporation of uncertainties, resulting in robust parameter constraints even in challenging cases with limited or ambiguous data. Consequently, our method successfully recovers case parameters for 19 systems, supplementary estimates for 8 systems, and identifies anomalies in 6 systems, including refined mass ratios and the identification of additional features such as caustic crossings in KMTALENJ, PST, TWH, KCH, and KMTGON. Collaborations with external groups yielded complete mass estimates for nine planets.

Differentiable rendering has gained significant attention in image-based inverse problems due to its potential to improve other optimization methods, although its widespread adoption is hindered by non-differentiable image operations such as shadow computation, which do not have an efficient way to calculate backward differences. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel, efficient method for computing shadows, compatible with modern rendering techniques, and present a closed-form analytic formula for a shadow function commonly used in recent research. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on various problems and observe that using the modern shadow function results in faster convergence and more accurate solutions compared to traditional methods. Additionally, our method facilitates the integration of shadow functions in differentiable image-based inverse problem solvers.

Recent research on transportation network demand estimation has shifted from predicting the average daily demand to tracking day-to-day demand estimation. Building on this progress, this paper develops estimation methods for origin-destination demand patterns by applying statistical inference. The method leverages gathered traffic statistics from a day-to-day estimation algorithm. Theoretical analysis proves that any origin-destination demand pattern can be estimated with precision, and further research shows that the estimation algorithm achieves consistent results as sample sizes increase. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated through numerical experiments using synthetic data.

In an array of nonlinear oscillators with random frequencies and purely conserved interactions, global phase coherence is demonstrated to occur within finite networks and further examined as it collapses through localized clusters or 'quasi-crystals'. Although these models have conserved interactions, they exhibit a strong analogy to phases with gradients, offering insight into the dynamics of more complex networks with conserved coupling.

The well-documented Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms create random spanning trees through random walks, and this paper examines the relationship between their outputs and proposes a two-stage approach to generating uniform spanning trees. Andsager will demonstrate that these algorithms can be seen as a unified method for a specific number of steps, and derive a new algorithm for generating spanning trees over multiple time intervals. This novel algorithm operates by combining the outputs of multiple random walks for specific numbers of steps and has been shown to produce uniform spanning trees. Additionally, the paper explores the covering times achieved by these walks over multiple time intervals.

This work presents a comprehensive dataset named MusicTM-Dataset to promote diverse model designs that can process sheet music, lyrics, and audio simultaneously.  This dataset comprises a rare collection of musicTM with matching sheet music, lyrics, and audio, enabling one to develop, test, and compare model designs that work with sheet music, lyrics, and audio.  This dataset can support a variety of advanced model designs that combine the information from sheet music, lyrics, and audio.  This dataset is feature-rich, offering high-quality sheet music, precise lyrics, and high-fidelity audio.  The sheet music in MusicTM-Dataset is annotated with musical symbols, making it possible to perform feature extraction.  This dataset is appropriate for multiple tasks, including musicTM representation learning, automatic musicTM retrieval, and the creation of musicTM generation models.  The dataset contains 1,753 training tracks, 50 validation tracks, and 50 query tracks with detailed metadata.  The dataset can be accessed at https://github.com/Fei-FeiLi/MusicTM-Dataset.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in navigating and comprehending the extensive list of properties associated with an entity, which can be daunting and time-consuming. To address this challenge, this paper presents an approach to identifying property similarities by analyzing entity-property patterns. By doing so, we aim to enhance data exploration experience of users, which can include tasks such as filtering or sorting. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, we applied it to the Wikidata dataset, which contains over 50 million items and more than 300,00 properties. In particular, we applied a word2vec word-embeddings model to explore the properties related to artistic movements, which we then validated through investigations on Wikipedia and Wikidata. To make our findings accessible, we developed a visual data exploration interface based on the Ontodia visual query language and integrated Wikidata as a semantic data source.

We've discovered that in systems with automatically adjusted dispersion, optical black solitons can switch between two stable forms when their energy is low, a phenomenon that contrasts with regular optical solitons which only exhibit one stable form, a phenomenon that makes sense given their differing shapes.

Within the realm of visual analytics, interactive and adaptable processes are gaining prominence for their versatility and adaptability. To tackle complex problems, various methods such as demand-driven and supply-driven processes are employed. Nonetheless, real-world applications often necessitate a harmonious blend of both approaches. Presenting 'Lotse', a framework designed to facilitate guided interactions within the visual analytics pipeline. Lotse empowers users to initiate their analysis independently, subsequently offering expert-recommended processes tailored to their current actions. Users can seamlessly integrate this framework into their workflow via a straightforward API, offering valuable insights into the full visual analytics pipeline. Its efficacy is demonstrated through an implementation that covers the full pipeline, coupled with a detailed analysis of use cases and a discussion on future possibilities.

We've developed an innovative approach to optimizing the shape of stellarators. Our method enables us to refine the shape of stellarators while maintaining them in a quasi-symmetric state across various rotational transform values and different vacuum coil designs. A crucial discovery from our research is that the shape of the stellarator required to achieve quasi-symmetry can be consistently described using a set of fundamental building blocks, or '母线圈', which can be easily reproduced and are capable of producing desirable quasi-symmetric properties. Our method's effectiveness is exemplified by the optimization of an advanced stellarator concept, where we found that our method can efficiently design a high-performance device following initial designs created using our '母线圈'.

Our research employs an innovative approach, utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in the protons T2* relaxation time-modality, to investigate temperature variations within a gas-solid fixed bed. By calibrating MRI's T2* parameters against actual temperatures, we've established a method to determine temperature distribution inside the bed. Temperature maps generated through MRI scanning are synchronized with infrared thermography images to validate our findings, revealing consistent temperature patterns in the bed. Using numerical correction for magnetic inhomogeneities, we eliminate temperature-related changes in T2* and analyze the temperature profile through axial slices. This approach enables analysis of axial and radial temperature variations, ultimately allowing estimation of overall bed temperature, as demonstrated in a batch reactor packed with fixed beds and a pharmaceutical substance.

Within a cellular environment, proteins and nucleic acids form membraneless droplets through a process of liquid-liquid phase separation. This phenomenon underpins the formation of various biological condenses, including the P-body, stress granule, and the P granule. Bicomodal droplets, composed of two distinct phases, have also been observed in certain P-granules. In this paper, a theoretical framework is developed to understand bicomodal droplets, which form through the self-assembly of multiple components, where some components drive the creation of one phase and another component drives the creation of a second phase. Adding further complexity to this process is the incorporation of a third substance that mediates interactions within both phases. Using a lattice-based model inspired by the Ising model, we identified a set of parameters leading to bicomodal droplets and outlined methods for determining these parameters. Next, a continuum model based on Landau-Freeman is developed to simplify the analysis and identification of parameters leading to bicomodal droplets. Our findings demonstrate that such structures can emerge through assemblies of two sets of components where each set selectively interacts within a phase and binds to a mediating substance. Our work also shows that whether a given mediating substance facilitates the creation of a bicomodal droplet depends on whether its concentration falls within a certain optimal range. Our study is relevant to understanding bicomodal droplets, where researchers can utilize our framework to identify key factors, including in the P-gran

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how a major leading sunspot rotated in NOAA AR 11429 during two powerful solar flares. A notable sunspot rotated in an unconventional direction, influenced significantly by the solar eruptions. Moving disturbances within other sunspots, caused by the solar flares, traveled rapidly and altered the magnetic properties of the sunspot group. Changes in the sunspot group's configuration, triggered by the solar flares and associated jets, created a complex and dynamic magnetic structure.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as $T$-independent, which forms the basis of an updated version of the b-principle. This updated version replaces Kotschick's prior application of the Mumford Conjecture on the homotopy of the mapping class group.

This research involves comparing the performance of different preconditioners for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems. These preconditioned iterative solvers speed up the solution process by efficient handling of matrix equations. A previously introduced multilevel preconditioner has shown promising results. This research takes the evaluation further. Various preconditioners are tested on two dimensional cardiac models, some of which replicate the properties of actual human tissue, on various cardiac simulation platforms. Furthermore, a novel preconditioner has been developed for computing the electrical signals in the heart. This logical advance allows for resolving larger scale electrical simulations with improved computational efficiency. A numerical analysis shows that the new preconditioner matches existing methods in 2D, and exhibits potential for use in 3D electrical simulations as well as mechanical simulations.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, driven in part by the proliferation of systems supporting content creation, sharing, and management. Among these systems are tag-based platforms that enable users to collaborate in annotating shared items such as images and URLs, leading to user-generated metadata pools and collaborative behavior. To unlock this potential, a comprehensive understanding of current systems is required, which involves characterizing these systems based on usage patterns, the evolution of user-generated content over time, the sharing of user interest, and collaborative behavior.

Recently, sub-wavelength acoustic metamaterials called metagratings have garnered significant interest, primarily due to their ability to outperform traditional acoustic materials, specifically in acoustic wave manipulation. Leveraging advanced two-photon polymerization technology, we have created high-performance metagratings capable of operating at ultrasonic frequencies between 3.75 and 4.5 GHz. By exploiting precise structural designs and leveraging numerical simulations, we have achieved remarkable control and manipulation of both longitudinal and flexural waves within a thin-layered system.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. By analyzing the decay rates of the linear system, we utilize a combination of the energy method and a careful examination of small initial disturbances. Our analysis demonstrates the decay of the $L^p$ norm over time, particularly the decay rate of the $H^2$ norm. Through the application of a compactness argument, we extend this result to arbitrary positive initial conditions, ultimately proving that the solution approaches a quiescent state as time goes to infinity.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) in mobile networks through wireless backhaul (WB) holds great potential for deploying dense network configurations with various benefits. However, the limitations of WB, specifically low data rates, limited range and poor quality of service (QoS) management, pose significant challenges when transporting control and backhaul traffic. To address these issues, we propose a solution using WB paving the way with paving agents (PAs) that mitigate these limitations by enhancing data rate and range while improving QoS. PAs function by dynamically adjusting wireless links to achieve optimal performance and maximize overall IAB network efficiency. To this end, we formulate a multi-objective optimization problem and develop an innovative two-phase algorithm - the CAscading Pi-based Algorithm for WB Paving (CASP) - to implement this idea. The CSPA algorithm involves a pilot phase where we determine the optimal number of PAs and their global positions, as well as a cascading phase where we optimize the number and placement of additional PAs, fine-tuning their parameters for maximum performance gain.

In this study, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of how hyperparameters in Evolutionary Algorithms (EAs) affect their effectiveness and efficiency, using global sensitivity analysis methods. This is the first time such an evaluation has been performed on the classic EA (EA-01) from the benchmark suite EA-01 to EA-09, where we compare the impact of different hyperparameter configurations and identify which ones are most relevant. The results not only provide insight into the importance of certain parameters, but also into the importance of other, less obvious factors, such as the problem's importance and the choice of effect measurement and effect estimator. The findings from this study have important implications for the field of EA research, where past research has often been based on the assumption that certain hyperparameter settings are universally optimal, while the current study suggests that no such settings exist and that the choice of hyperparameters should be made based on the specific problem at hand.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently compares the time evolution of this configuration with the decomposition of a solution to the wave equation, highlighting that these solutions converge under the given constraints. The analysis is extended to demonstrate how a charge and current moving at constant velocity generate electromagnetic fields consistent with the boosted fields obtained through Lorentz transformation.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain to be cleared before achieving consistent performance, particularly when dealing with novel, continuously evolving problems. Researchers have developed novel assessment frameworks to evaluate transfer and lifelong learning abilities, though their limited problem sets restrict their broader applicability. In response to this, we introduce L2Explorer, an open-source Python framework, featuring a collection of 27 interconnected environments drawn from diverse robotics domains. This collection, along with our accompanying paper, aims to drive further innovation in reinforcement learning problem design and facilitate FDR design. Specifically, we provide a detailed description of our L2Explorer L2Dynamical assessment framework for fluid dynamics, including its objective, methodology, and initial analysis results. Additionally, we include a comprehensive review of 27 individual tasks within our environment collection to drive further development in the areas of transfer, continual, and generative learning.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, features 166 1kx1k amorphous Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide (IGZO) spacers and offers exceptional sensitivity, high dynamic range, and a vast field of view. To maximize its full potential, Liger will consist of 16 cameras with customized optical systems, each requiring a customized data reduction system to process data efficiently. To address this challenge, we will develop a customized data reduction system for Liger that can effectively handle data from multiple cameras, ensuring optimal performance and ease of use. To facilitate this, we will utilize a versatile and adaptable pipeline based on the irpipe framework, while also designing a custom interface to simplify the data reduction process. To meet these requirements, we will leverage open-source and in-house developed software, including a customized data reduction system based on the irpipe framework, as well as other specialized tools to process data efficiently.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth traveling wave patterns in 2D Euler equation solutions, existing in close proximity to the Couette flow vector field. Our analysis shows that their associated velocity fields have a smooth, periodic, and two-dimensional caustic structure, and we also identify an infinite set of unique, smooth, and traveling wave patterns in 2D Euler equation solutions, featuring a specific symmetry, with velocity fields exhibiting two distinct modes.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a unique method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local gradient components. The specific focus lies within a class of non-local problems set in a finite-dimensional space with a given domain. The equation format is a modification of a previously formulated equation in this space, with a new term added to the right side. The variation is also extensible to higher dimensions with grid-based non-local operators applied. The study is further expanded to include comparisons with other non-local problems and a discussion of implications for higher-dimensional equations.

The 2019 novel coronavirus outbreak is the first to be tracked in the COVID-19 era, with the World Health Organization providing real-time statistics on infected and deceased individuals from various countries. In response, South Africa set up the National Coronavirus Task Force in March 2020 to manage the pandemic, announcing a daily press briefing to disclose patient information and implement necessary measures to mitigate its spread. This research examined whether the task force's strategic decisions were influenced by domestic data, including imported cases, deaths, and infected individuals, as well as whether such influence resulted in a decrease in deaths or a drop in new infections. Using time series analysis, we discovered a significant correlation between exogenous variables and strategic decisions, suggesting that the task force's data-driven approach may have contributed to South Africa's relatively low death rate and infection rate, achieving a death rate comparable to neighboring countries, despite not reporting cases, deaths, or infected individuals.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem, a fundamental result, states that any set of at least 2k elements containing fewer than k non-sums of pairs from the set can be encompassed within a subset of at most 4k elements that forms an arithmetic progression.

We've further strengthened this result by demonstrating that if a set of elements from at least k available options for each pair of indices from the set of size at least k elements, can be included in a subset of at most 4k elements that forms an arithmetic progression.

Deep neural networks have revolutionized the diagnosis of retinal diseases, particularly in the early detection of retinal disorders. Recent studies on retinal disease detection emphasize the importance of multi-task learning and feature extraction from fundus images. In contrast, there is a relative scarcity of research into retinal information fusion for the diagnosis of retinopathy. This work addresses this gap by proposing a novel, efficient deep neural network architecture for a novel, two-stage approach that combines structural information from 2D images and multi-channel frequency-domain information. The proposed method is evaluated on a public dataset of retinal fundus images and demonstrates superior performance compared to a state-of-the-art baseline, achieving higher accuracy in the difficult task of glaucoma detection.

X-ray images of the lungs can reveal specific patterns indicative of COVID-19 severity, specifically the likelihood of ICU admission.  This likelihood can be captured through distinct features visible on X-ray images, including areas of intense infection, paths of infection spread, overall lung involvement, and geographic concentration factors. This study aims to identify how these features visible on X-ray images relate to the risk of ICU admission, by training a model to detect this risk and analyzing which features it uses to make its decision. This model was trained using a large dataset of X-ray images, labeled with the severity of the patients, and was found to accurately predict the risk of ICU admission. This model was then found to rely on specific features visible on X-ray images to make its decision, by using a model attribution technique. This model attribute analysis revealed that the model likely predicts ICU admission based on the presence of intense patterns, patterns that spread, overall lung involvement scores, and geographic concentration factors, by viewing samples of X-ray images and manually verifying these features' presence. This model attribute analysis also found that these features are relevant to the risk of ICU admission, by using a model-agnostic feature importance technique. This model importance analysis found that the most impactful feature is the intensity factor, as it contributed the most to accurate ICU admission predictions, while other features, including patterns that spread, overall lung involvement scores, and geographic concentration factors, also contributed to accurate ICU admission predictions. We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem involving $n$-dimensional
spherically symmetric and layered media. As the index $n$ increases beyond
two, our research reveals that the transmission eigenfunctions highly localize
at the boundary of a specific interface, denoted as $r=r_0$. This means that the
eigenfunctions' transmission coefficient approaches zero. Furthermore, our
research indicates that the eigenvalues' transmission coefficients also
decrease exponentially with the eigenvalue index $k$, particularly for $k$ being
much larger than the eigenvalue $λ$. This study builds on previous works and
extends their scope to apply to any number of dimensions $n$ and includes additional
analyses of eigenvalue behavior.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities, discovering new intent categories is crucial. This paper presents a novel pre-trained model, which discovers new intents by identifying patterns in a feature space, rather than relying on labeled data. We achieve this pre-training by introducing two techniques: 1) denoising autoencoding to preserve original input, and 2) contrastive learning that identifies similar utterances from different domains. Our pre-trained model enhances both flexibility and performance when fine-tuning on labeled data. For unsupervised new intent discovery, it identifies similar samples by mapping them into a unified space, and our proposed pre-training boosts their accuracy. We evaluate our approach using two benchmarks and demonstrate its effectiveness in new intent discovery, as well as its transferability across labeled datasets.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme's four-potential, which can be expressed through line integrals of its 1-form. The study delves into the dependencies of this 1-form and finds that for most cases, it is not a exact 1-form. The study identifies exceptions to this general rule, which occur when the matrix script S is either a constant or a function of the matrix script R, with a specific condition on script R. The study identifies new exact 1-forms with S depending on script R, which were previously unknown. Additionally, the study explores the properties of these 1-forms, which are either periodic or expressible as single-valued functions, and finds that these properties lead to new equations with the Adler-Bobenko-Hong equation as a particular case.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discover that the relationship and object proposals generated by the detector are often redundant, as indicated by the loss functions. This redundancy hampers the model's ability to learn accurate relationships, leading to a decline in performance and a rise in false positives. To address this issue, we introduce a novel framework called Progress-Gated VRL. This framework incrementally activates various components in multi-task networks, allowing each module time to learn its individual task before taking on additional tasks. By doing so, we minimize the impact of competing tasks on each other, ultimately leading to more accurate relationship proposals and a lower false positive rate. This new framework is particularly effective in mitigating the challenges associated with data imbalance and competing tasks, as evidenced by our experimental results which show significant improvement in VRD, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods on COCO-VR and HR-VR datasets.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, quantum correlations can be extracted even when classical correlations are absent in a system. Additionally, the QCC is found to be more expansive compared to the local orthogonality quantity (LOP) in certain instances.

Artificial intelligence is making significant advancements in simulating social interactions, bringing greater life to virtual agents in gaming and digital world by generating socially connected avatars. Recent breakthroughs have focused on efficiently describing individual agents' characteristics, but there's a lack of research on creating a comprehensive network of social relationships. In contrast, this paper develops a neural network capable of simultaneously generating a social relationship map and its associated user profiles, where each user is represented as a central node, and their connections, as relational edges, are defined by a symmetric matrix. The framework's architecture uses two interconnected GNN-based modules to create shared representations of individual users, which then determine the social relationship matrix and the user profile.

Graph-structured data is ubiquitous but existing graph neural networks (GNNs) are primarily designed to handle static graphs, limiting their application to scenarios involving such structures. However, many real-world situations involve scenarios with dynamic graphs, characterized by changing topology over time. To bridge this ap-lication gap, this study introduces the Dynamic Graph Message Passing Network (D-GMPN), a new GNN architecture that overcomes current method-ological obstacles in addressing dynamic graphs. Notably, D-GMPN messages are formulated to preserve the Markov property, enabling effective learning from incomplete observations of a dynamic graph. In addition, a new GMPN message update method is proposed to efficiently adapt to changing graphs without becoming trapped in local optima. To further enhance performance, a D-GMPN model is presented that seamlessly accommodates varying graph structures. Experimental results on a diverse set of recognition tasks validate the D-GMPN's superior-ity and demonstrate its broad applicability in visual recognition.

Optimized hardware is crucial for optimized circuit design, and optimizing complex and frequent operations like Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) can lead to improved Simple Instruction Single Data (SISD) architectures, making them more efficient. A novel and automatic approach to MCM optimization has been proposed, leveraging Python and the PyMCM framework to offer a user-friendly interface for designing and implementing efficient MAC units. This new algorithm integrates existing techniques and introduces innovative solutions, such as a new [D, W] pair optimization algorithm and a generalized mapping algorithm, to explore a wide range of possible mappings and retain them for future better MAC hardware optimizations. Comprehensive simulations have validated the efficacy of the PyMCM algorithm, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the design of MAC hardware.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radiofrequency accelerator technology is a well-established technology, 
enabling significant size compactness and reliable beam delivery with precise timing. 
This is achieved through high brightness particle production, typically in the charge per pulse range of $10^6$ to $10^8$, and high repetition rates, typically between $100$ Hz and $100$ kHz. 
The primary areas of research and development focus on increasing the beam power handling, interacting with target materials, and enhancing the radiation safety due to increased repetition rates. 
The increased radiation also leads to accelerated component degradation, posing additional technical hurdles. 
Given the need for high reliability in particle generation, typical in 99.99%, the R&D efforts prioritize risk mitigation and high reliability in particle production. 
This paper will delve into the current technology, challenges, and potential opportunities in acceleration technology, specifically targeting electrons and photons, while leaving hadronic particle production for a subsequent discussion.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the machine and its detector environment.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows correspondence with first-order causal theories and highlights how a specific divergence-based model can predict damped tensor waves. This aligns with kinetic theory's results. It's interesting that both hydrodynamic and holographic fluids display anionic dispersion for certain modes. Our findings suggest that a simple two-parameter relaxation-time approximation can effectively model the hydrodynamic behavior of quark-gluon plasma produced in heavy-ion collisions.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes (PBHs) could be the source behind the observed radio events in the Fast Radio Burst (FRB) sky. A 2023 study proposed that an PBH collapse could trigger a brief, intense flash of gamma rays and high-energy particles, potentially explaining FRBs. In a subsequent process, the resulting black hole emits Hawking radiation, primarily in the form of low-energy photons. If this PBH-driven Hawking radiation is within detectable frequency ranges, it has the potential to contribute to the radio sky's intensity. To further investigate, we have modelled the radio emission from a single PBH, taking into account its evolving emission rates as it loses mass. To our knowledge, this consideration is new to the study of Hawking radiation, which typically assumes static emission. By comparing our models to the FRB 20220628V2 data, which shows repeated bursts, varying spectra, and evolving rates, we have determined that a single PBH cannot fully account for these observations. However, a cloud of PBHs, where a fraction collapse to trigger radio bursts, could potentially produce the observed patterns. To constrain this possibility, we have used the FRB 20220628V2 data to set an upper limit of approximately $2\times 10^{23}\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a cutting-edge solution for securing computation within an untrusted environment. VSP is a five-stage pipeline processor built atop a 3D memory hierarchy, specifically designed to secure computation over the Tensor-FHE (TFHE) scheme, enabling secure operation across its hierarchical components. As a secure platform, VSP is engineered to secure communication, data storage, and program execution across its subsystems, featuring a secure multi-stage pipeline architecture, hierarchical memory structure, and robust security protocols, with the ultimate goal of securing computation within its localized environment.

VSP is composed of five stages: fetch, decode, read, execute, and write, each containing secure modules responsible for specific functions, with the execute stage comprising a secure and reconfigurable execution unit (SEU) capable of executing secure code written in VDL, featuring a custom instruction set and secure data handling capabilities. VSP is built over RISC-V, a modern, open-standard architecture designed for security, scalability, and efficiency, with the execute stage incorporating a secure RISC-V core as its SEU.

VSP is an innovative solution for securing computation within a virtualized environment, combining a customized, secure version of a modern architecture and a 3D memory hierarchy for specific workloads. We've developed a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for a broad category of constraint satisfaction problems. A specific instance of such a problem, known as a CSP, involves selecting objects from sets with limited or sparse elements to optimize a weighted function. We've proven that this value can be achieved within a factor of at most $(1+\epsilon)$ for any positive value of $\epsilon$ on any instance of such a CSP that meets certain constraints. Furthermore, we've shown that by applying a localized search technique, our PTAS can be executed in $O\bigl(n^{1 + O(\frac{\log n}{\delta^2\epsilon^2})}\bigr)$ time, where $\delta$ represents the maximum size of its constraint. We've also shown that for instances with a finite number of elements in their sets, we can achieve an $O\bigl(n^{1+o(1)}\bigr)$ time running for an $\epsilon$-approximation. We've also analyzed the feasibility of PTAs and found that by adapting Goemans and Williamson's PTAS for the maximum cut problem, we've established that by assuming P does not equal NP, we've established that for some finite sets and positive integers $k$, there exists a PTAS whose time running is $O\bigl(n^{k}\bigr)$.

Pre-trained language models have the potential to significantly improve parsing models, given their ability to provide an in-depth understanding of language. However, few-shot parsing models, including the pre-trained ones, struggle with providing an accurate and consistent representation of a language's syntax, particularly when it comes to capturing the structural relationships between words. Our research addresses this limitation by developing a new parsing approach based on tree-structured semi-markov dependencies. Our proposed approach can learn pre-trained parsing models without any annotated data, and can achieve state-of-the-art results with only a small amount of training data. Moreover, we introduce a novel long-term dependency loss that significantly enhances the quality of the pre-trained parsing models, leading to substantial improvements in the accuracy of the extracted syntax structures. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in several ways: first, few-shot parsing models based on pre-trained language models are now possible, outperforming other models with access to extensive amounts of training data; second, these models have reached an unprecedented level of accuracy, with a CoNLL parsing accuracy of 98.25% achieved by the F1-score, which is only 0.42 below the accuracy of the best possible accuracy of 97.82.

High-precision applications like autonomous driving and 3D modeling rely on detailed knowledge of urban environments, which is provided by advanced semantic segmentation techniques. This process involves accurately categorizing different objects in an image, a task that is made easier by combining various data sources. We propose a method for weakly-supervised training of this process using hyperspectral data, which is easier to obtain and comes with a coarse segmentation mask. This method leverics the precise labeling information in the mask to create a detailed activation map from the hyperspectral data. We design a multi-scale feature extraction network that helps the model learn detailed features from the mask and produce accurate activations that can be compared with the network's original input image. This approach allows us to refine the activation map and generate final predictions that can be used for easy comparison with the coarse mask in the loss function. Our method achieves competitive results in vehicle and pedestrian detection in the Cityscape dataset, as well as overall performance when compared to existing strong activation re-ranking techniques.

This study presents compelling evidence of a K-type giant star exhibiting extreme rotation, notably faster than anticipated based on standard stellar evolution expectations. We analyzed high-quality spectroscopic data obtained through the VLT's SINFOS instrument and employed the Splitting Broadening Language to measure rotational broadening and macroturbulence. Unlike typical slowly rotating K giants, this unusual star displayed a rotational broadening parameter of 13.2% with a corresponding macroturbulence parameter of only 10.3%, significantly diverging from the usual pattern. Notably, it resembles a rare class of rapidly rotating red giant stars that exhibit signs of planetary engulfment. We present a plausible model in which a close encounter and ingestion of a large planet accelerated the star's rotation, an idea supported by existing evidence. Alternatively, we discuss other possible explanations, such as the presence of a distant companion star or unusual internal angular momentum transfer, though we find these scenarios to be less likely.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. However, key RAM model assumptions, such as the cost of arithmetic operations, can significantly influence algorithm analysis. While many algorithms rely on efficient multiplication and division, their actual performance in the RAM model may not always be reflected by their analytical bounds. This research focuses on determining which basic arithmetic operations can be performed in constant time within a one-based RAM model that only supports addition, and the results show that for unbounded RAMs, algorithms for subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder can all be implemented in constant time. Notably, these findings apply equally to unbounded and bounded RAMs, as long as the word size is unbounded in both cases.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative method in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by projecting invariant differential forms defined on the graph complexes of Feynman type as per Goncharov's work. The invariant differential forms on the graphs of Feynman type serve as explicit representatives for the homology of the absolute values of the graph field, a concept introduced by Denef-Loeser and Goncharov. Following this, we relate our projective forms to a graph model of the absolute convergent integrals, a model proposed by Brown. These projective forms allow evaluation at the boundary strata, thereby providing expression of each integral as a linear combination of these forms, enabling their asymptotic expansion with graph-based coefficients.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  By training RNNs on an object recognition task and analyzing their internal structures, we discovered that the representation of individual objects can be decomposed into two distinct components: one that is orthogonal to other objects and another that shares similarities with them.  These components, when combined, enhance the network's ability to overcome ambiguity in learning, thereby improving its performance in object categorization tasks.

Despite significant progress in understanding topological phases of interacting systems, the correlation effects on topological properties remain an open question. We address this issue by exploring the impact of correlations in one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems with linear quench, a scenario where a chiral symmetry protects the topological phase and drives the system into a unique many-body eigenstate. We observe that the topological index, which signifies the system's topological property, is reduced by approximately half due to correlation effects and shows a logarithmic decline as the system size expands. We attribute this decline to the increasing influence of boundary states, which are more accessible due to the anomalous dimension associated with the L\'evy flight process, a phenomenon where the system occasionally jumps longer distances than the system size.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity as a way to expand the known sets of Golay complementary phasor arrays. This paper explores a new method for creating multicore optical systems that exhibit Golay complementary properties, thereby increasing the total capacity these systems can achieve. This new method utilizes all available degrees of freedom - core, mode, and frequency - in such optical systems to maximize their potential.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC, specifically the four-lepton final state, for a total of 137 fb^-1. By analyzing both on- and off-shell Higgs boson decays, multiple off-shell production and decay assumptions are evaluated against the standard model model, ultimately yielding no significant deviation. An integrated estimate of the Higgs boson width is found to be around 3.71 MeV, with confidence at 95%, or about seven times the standard model model prediction. Additionally, certain HVV coupling coefficients were evaluated, with multiple off-shell production and decay assumptions being tested, ultimately yielding no significant deviation. An integrated estimate of HVV coupling coefficients was found to range from -0.0024 to -0.0024, with confidence at 95%, or about eight times the standard model model prediction.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands in change detection tasks. This study introduces a novel approach using a deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across various levels of detail. By doing so, it effectively captures both subtle and significant changes within the data. By unsupervisedly learning from the unsynchronized spectral data, this method effectively eliminates the need for spectral alignment. By evaluating common unsupervised change detection metrics on synthetic and real-world datasets, our proposed method demonstrates superior performance on real data, outshining existing state-of-the-art methods.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$, defined as all square numbers, and let $\mathcal{C}$ be a set containing all natural numbers that cannot be expressed as the sum of a square number and another element from the set $\mathcal{C}$. This implies that the sum of any two elements from the set $\mathcal{C}$ is not a square number. The goal is to find the largest possible value of the set $\mathcal{C}$, measured by its natural logarithm in comparison to its natural logarithm of $n$. A similar problem was solved previously, where the set of square numbers was replaced with that of prime numbers.

Quantum tunneling is a phenomenon in which a particle bypasses an energy barrier due to its wave-like properties, and it plays a crucial role in various quantum mechanical effects. When two or more wave components bypass a barrier, they can interfere with each other, and this phenomenon can be utilized to study and manipulate the properties of matter. In this study, lattice imaging was performed on spin-polarized silicon, and an interference pattern was observed, which is attributed to valley interference caused by an L-valley electron. Furthermore, image contrast associated with a hydrogen atom was found to depend on its orientation, and this was attributed to spin exchange between the hydrogen atom and surrounding silicon. These findings demonstrate valley interference for the first time and suggest spin precession mediated by hydrogen, which can be used to study and manipulate valley and spin degrees of freedom in silicon.

A wide range of optimization techniques, such as quadratic programming and
infinite-dimensional optimization, have now been applied in various electronic
design automation (EDA) fields. However, due to the absence of a comprehensive
and easily accessible toolset, exploiting these optimization techniques for EDA
problems has been challenging. In response, we present a flexible, modular, and
easy-to-use software framework for EDAs, called LibOPT, which enables the rapid
development and evaluation of novel optimization methods and applications.
LibOPT's algorithm library, library, and accompanying example applications allow
users to integrate and compare various optimization methods and applications,
including circuit design, to quickly obtain valuable insights. In addition, our
framework is designed to be intuitive and straightforward, making it a valuable
asset for the research community. By providing a rich set of features and the
capability for easy extension, LibOPT serves as a valuable platform for
experimentation and helps to drive innovation in the field of EDAs through the
effective use of optimization techniques.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time, the properties of space are defined by a matrix that does not commute, and these properties are defined by a matrix called $	heta_{\mu
u}$. We show that for non-commutative quantum particles, the identity of the particles is lost in the traditional sense, and redefined by the properties of the matrix $	heta_{\mu
u}$. The mathematical description of the particles is based on deformed algebra and can be expressed as a special type of equation, resulting in the loss of the particles' individuality, and the emergence of identical states for exchange. As a result, the properties of the particles resemble a special type of fermions, and the properties of the particles resemble a special type of super-statistics. However, for small values of the matrix $	heta_{\mu
u}$, the particles behave as separate, distinguishable entities, and for high values of the matrix $	heta_{\mu
u}$ the particles become identical for exchange, resulting in a loss of the particles' individuality, and the emergence of a special type of fermions, and the properties of the particles resemble a special type of super-statistics.
